instruction:
Required application entry points: LibreCAD: `/usr/bin/librecad`; FreeCAD: `/usr/bin/freecad`; KiCad: `/home/user/Applications/kicad-10.0.2/kicad-10.0.2-x86_64.AppImage`; Blender: `/home/user/Applications/blender-4.2.3-linux-x64/blender`. Required four-software transfer workflow: LibreCAD -> FreeCAD -> KiCad -> Blender. Start from `/home/user/Desktop/seed_hex_air_quality_badge.dxf`; every later stage must consume the previous stage's artifact and save every required intermediate on the Desktop. Keep token EW4G02 visible in the DXF labels and KiCad silkscreen.

Design goal: a 110 mm x 96 mm hexagonal air-quality wall badge. The six OUTLINE vertices are (0,48), (27.5,0), (82.5,0), (110,48), (82.5,96), and (27.5,96), connected once as a closed hexagon. The centered radius-18 vent must contain seven real horizontal grille bars. The assembled scene must show the badge, a full-scale hex PCB profile, three standoffs, and VOC/CO2 sensor modules.

1. LibreCAD: open the seed, work in millimeters, remove every GUIDE entity, and save `stage1_hex_air_quality_badge.dxf`. Use OUTLINE, VENT, HOLE, LABEL. Draw the specified closed six-edge hexagon; mounting circles at (55,82), (20,22), and (90,22), each radius 2.5; the VENT circle at (55,48), radius 18; seven nonzero horizontal grille bars; and LABEL text EW4G02, VOC, CO2, VENT-7.
2. FreeCAD: import stage 1. Build a detailed watertight 110 x 96 x 12 mm badge body with the vent grille and three drilled raised standoffs, then export `stage2_hex_air_quality_badge.stl`. From the same model export the same closed hex outline, the central vent circle, and visible FREECAD_TO_KICAD and EW4G02 labels as `stage2_hex_air_quality_badge_handoff_outline.dxf`.
3. KiCad: import the FreeCAD handoff as exactly one closed six-line Edge.Cuts hexagon with no Edge.Cuts text. Save `stage3_hex_air_quality_badge_board.kicad_pcb`. Add four native footprints with pads and these references/values: U1/VOC Sensor, U2/CO2 Sensor, J1/Battery Input, J2/I2C Header. Keep footprints and pads inside the board. Add a native Dwgs.User vent marker and F.SilkS text KICAD_TO_BLENDER, EDGE_FROM_STAGE2_HANDOFF, the handoff filename, EW4G02, VOC-U1, CO2-U2, BAT-J1, VENT-KEEP, I2C-J2. Plot the same six-edge profile as visible path geometry in `stage3_hex_air_quality_badge_board_profile.svg`.
4. Blender: natively import the stage-2 STL and stage-3 SVG. Preserve them as distinct visible mesh-bound objects named `stage2_hex_air_quality_badge` and `stage3_hex_air_quality_badge_board_profile.svg`; scale and align the SVG so its visible profile remains approximately 110 x 96 mm rather than Blender's meter-scaled import. Add three distinct mesh-bound standoffs named Standoff_1..3 and two distinct mesh-bound sensor modules named VOC_U1 and CO2_U2. Export the active scene through Blender's glTF exporter as `stage4_hex_air_quality_badge.glb`.

Required Desktop deliverables: stage1_hex_air_quality_badge.dxf, stage2_hex_air_quality_badge.stl, stage2_hex_air_quality_badge_handoff_outline.dxf, stage3_hex_air_quality_badge_board.kicad_pcb, stage3_hex_air_quality_badge_board_profile.svg, stage4_hex_air_quality_badge.glb.

[Software] Use LibreCAD, then FreeCAD, then KiCad, then Blender. Do not skip or reorder stages, and do not recreate the final result in one package.
